knowledge:
- key_parameters: nBurnin=number of burn-in MCMC iterations in GGPA() ;; nMain=number of main MCMC iterations in GGPA() ;; FDR=nominal FDR level in assoc() ;; fdrControl=type of FDR control ("global" or "local") in assoc() ;; i=index of first phenotype of interest for joint association mapping in assoc() or fdr() ;; j=index of second phenotype of interest for joint association mapping in assoc() or fdr()
- alternatives: Standard GPA (without graph structure) or other multi-GWAS joint analysis methods. The docs mention that incorporating a prior disease graph (via DDNet) improves on the uninformative prior graph-GPA model.
- when_to_use: When analyzing multiple GWAS p-value datasets simultaneously to identify shared genetic variants (pleiotropy) and understand the genetic relationships (phenotype graph) among diseases/phenotypes.
- pitfalls: Using too few MCMC iterations (e.g., the default or vignette's 200/200) for real data; 10,000 burn-in and 40,000 main iterations are recommended. Mismatch between the columns/column names of the p-value matrix (pmat) and the prior graph (pgraph). They must match exactly.

workflows.name: standard_graph_gpa
workflows.intent: Fit a graph-GPA model to multiple GWAS p-value datasets to perform association mapping and estimate the phenotype graph without prior knowledge.
input: pmat (matrix of GWAS p-values where rows are SNPs and columns are phenotypes)
workflows.stages: 1. Fit the graph-GPA model using GGPA ;; 2. Extract parameter estimates using estimates ;; 3. Perform marginal and joint association mapping using assoc ;; 4. Calculate local FDR using fdr ;; 5. Visualize the estimated phenotype graph using plot
workflows.code:
set.seed(12345)
fit <- GGPA( simulation$pmat, nBurnin=200, nMain=200 )
fit
str(estimates(fit))
assoc.marg <- assoc( fit, FDR=0.10, fdrControl="global" )
dim(assoc.marg)
apply( assoc.marg, 2, table )
fdr.marg <- fdr(fit)
dim(fdr.marg)
head(fdr.marg)
assoc.joint <- assoc( fit, FDR=0.10, fdrControl="global", i=1, j=2 )
length(assoc.joint)
head(assoc.joint)
table(assoc.joint)
plot(fit)

workflows.name: graph_gpa_with_prior
workflows.intent: Fit a graph-GPA model incorporating an informative prior disease graph (e.g., downloaded from DDNet) to improve SNP prioritization and pleiotropic architecture estimation.
input: pmat (matrix of GWAS p-values where rows are SNPs and columns are phenotypes)
pgraph (adjacency matrix of the prior disease graph, sharing the same columns and column names as pmat)
workflows.stages: 1. Fit the graph-GPA model with the prior graph using GGPA ;; 2. Perform downstream association mapping and visualization using assoc, fdr, and plot
